title: Our Lady of Loreto (10 December)
hook: a shrine honoring the house of Nazareth, patron of pilots

segments.voice: Yesterday, Juan Diego, who asked to be replaced and was chosen anyway. Your line was the littlest son.

Rough stone walls. A small, plain room, the kind of room a family once lived in. And around it, a great church on a hilltop in Loreto, in central Italy, built to hold this one plain room like a jewel box holds a ring. Pilgrims shuffle in, touch the walls, and some kneel on the floor. Why would anyone build a basilica around a room this ordinary? Because of whose room, tradition says, it was.
screen: `A SMALL ROOM OF ROUGH STONE.` → `A GREAT CHURCH AROUND IT.` → `WHOSE ROOM WAS IT?`

segments.voice: Tradition holds that this is the house of Nazareth, the house of Mary, where the angel came to her. Luke's gospel sets the scene. In the Douay-Rheims: "the angel Gabriel was sent from God into a city of Galilee, called Nazareth." God's message lands not in a temple, but in a small town, in someone's home. Then comes the legend. The story says that when the house was in danger, angels lifted it and carried it through the air, setting it down at last on the hill at Loreto. Some historians suggest a plainer route: people, not angels, moving the stones and rebuilding them. The feast doesn't depend on settling that. What it honors is the house, and what happened in it. John's gospel says it in one line: "And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us." Dwelt. Lived somewhere. Had a door, a table, a floor that needed sweeping. For Catholics who pray at Loreto, the shrine is a way of touching that ordinary home where, they believe, the Son of God grew up. And the flying house had a modern sequel. Because of the legend, Our Lady of Loreto became the patron of pilots and air travelers, and some people still say a prayer to her before a flight. A litany of titles for Mary is named for this shrine, too: the Litany of Loreto, prayed there and far beyond.
screen: `THE HOUSE OF NAZARETH, TRADITION SAYS.` · `CARRIED BY ANGELS, THE LEGEND SAYS.` · `THE WORD DWELT AMONG US.` · `PATRON OF PILOTS AND TRAVELERS.` · then, large: `AND THE WORD WAS MADE FLESH.`

segments.voice: Right now, somewhere above you, planes are in the air: pilots watching their instruments, crews pouring coffee, passengers asleep against the window, someone flying home to a hospital bed, someone flying toward a new job. If you know someone traveling, hold them first, then widen it to everyone up there. If you pray, ask Our Lady of Loreto to watch over them; if you don't, wish them a safe landing, one face at a time.
Santa Casa. Mary honored at the shrine of the holy house, which tradition holds to be her home in Nazareth, and patron of those who fly.
Your line: the holy house. In the story, God came to an ordinary home. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Our Lady of Loreto is remembered on 10 December; pilgrims visit the Holy House inside the basilica at Loreto, and some air travelers and crews ask her protection before flights.
